scope: synthetic complete-family holdout; not a production vulnerability-detector claim
research_question: Can a fixed-size neural model learn URL trust semantics from abstract primitives without seeing any url_scheme_downgrade training example?

model.name: SIFT-0.9M URL Set Head
model.architecture_change: canonical URL slots plus a learned query-to-labeled-set comparison head

causal_chain.finding: The byte Transformer learned field and family shortcuts and did not reliably bind episode labels to URL components.
Canonical scheme, hostname, effective-port and path slots removed unstable source-field names.
URL-primitive-only meta-label permutation penalized fixed family-to-label shortcuts without perturbing unrelated families.
A 128-parameter learned set-comparison head supplied the missing query-to-positive/negative-example comparison bias.
Disabling only the set head in the same checkpoint cost at least 28.83 percentage points on both fresh seeds.

failed_branches.name: canonical slots plus global meta-label pilot
failed_branches.reason: 54.33% target accuracy; representation alone did not repair episode binding

failed_branches.name: global-meta set-head confirmation
failed_branches.reason: strong URL transfer but truthiness_gate regressed by 3.83pp, exceeding the preregistered 2pp limit

failed_branches.name: selective meta v1
failed_branches.reason: substring_origin regressed by 5.67pp because an unrelated family was still label-permuted

failed_branches.name: URL meta v2
failed_branches.reason: restricted meta-labeling to URL primitives and passed two untouched complete-family holdouts

separation_of_claims.neural: 88.42% mean on the unseen URL family; supported by same-checkpoint ablation
separation_of_claims.c5: 100% zero-parameter executable rule architecture; reported separately and not counted as neural learning
separation_of_claims.engineering: not yet established; requires broader languages, parsers, noise, real runtimes and operational reliability tests
